english: 175-179. These terrible ones carry away the infants still in the wombs or immediately after being born. These Śiśumātṛs (‘Infant Mothers’) are seven, viz. Kākī, Hilimā, Rudrā, Vṛṣabhā, Āyā, Palālā and Mitrā. The infant (Lord Kumara) enriched by the vigour and vitality of these (mothers) became excessively terrific. The son born as a result of the blessings of Skanda was the fearful Lohitākṣa. Thus the mysterious group of Skandamātṛs (named) Vīrāṣṭaka (‘eight heroic ones’) has been recounted. This group has to be devoutly worshipped always. It bestows, peace and calmness after subduing all types of Apasmāras (‘epileptic fits’). Śrī (‘glory and prosperity’) assumed a body and approached and served Skanda who had golden armour and necklace, who was clad in red robes and had youthful lustre, the most excellent one in all the three worlds. Śrī resorted to him herself and bowed down to him.
